messages:
raja: Quick thread — I ran a persistent-KV pager soak to compare paging/eviction behavior across regions/GPU types. Targets: h100/us-west1, a100/eu-west1, h100/apac. Sequence length mix = short(<=128):60%, med(129-512):30%, long(>512):10%. Root config: persistent pager, eviction=LRU-weighted, prefetch threshold=0.75. Charts uploaded to the bench bucket.

lin: Nice. What's the primary signal? hitrate vs p99 or paging bandwidth?

raja: both. Primary ops: measured cache hit rate, per-token p50/p95/p99, and background paging write/read bandwidth + eviction sweep latency. Observed region/GPU divergence — A100 in eu-west1 hit a lower kv hit rate at identical prefetch threshold and higher p99.

anya: Command I used to reproduce:
```
run_bench --model redwood-7b-q --gpu h100 --region us-west1 \
  --slen-mix short:0.6,med:0.3,long:0.1 \
  --pager persistent --evict lru-weighted --prefetch-threshold 0.75 \
  --duration 3600 --trace kv,latency
```

ml-ci-bot: Auto-summary: h100/us-west1: hit_rate=0.84, p50=12ms, p95=38ms, p99=72ms, paging_bw=420MB/s. a100/eu-west1: hit_rate=0.76, p50=14ms, p95=52ms, p99=118ms, paging_bw=260MB/s. h100/apac: hit_rate=0.81, p50=13ms, p95=44ms, p99=90ms. (details: s3://redwood-bench/persistent-kv/1862345678/)

sam: Interesting. A100 lower paging_bw explains part of p99. Also kernel choices differ — A100 job used cutlass/spmm path; H100 run used the fused-attn-backed kv memcpy which is slightly faster for our layout.

lin: Could quantization be affecting eviction heuristics? Did the q config change key size or serialized footprint?

anya: We tested 4-bit quant for the model; it reduced model size ~2.1x but increased token emission bursts (higher token-per-request variance) which slightly decreased observed hit rate on long sequences. Quality regression on eval set was ~0.8% (acceptable for some workloads) but throughput improved.

raja: So there are three interacting levers: (1) prefetch threshold per region/gpu, (2) eviction policy weight tuning for slen distribution, (3) kernel/driver tuning on A100 for paging bandwidth. Proposed grid: prefetch thresholds [0.6,0.7,0.8,0.85] x evict weight alpha [0.6,0.8,1.0] x kernel flag {cutlass,fused}. Run 30m per cell with same slen mix.

sam: +1. For eu-west1/A100, start with prefetch=0.6 and evict alpha=0.8. If paging_bw stays low, try increasing background IO threads or change NVMe staging chunk size.

ml-ci-bot: Enqueued matrix job "kv-pager-regional-grid-1862345678". Will post results once complete.

anya: I ran a microbench to measure eviction sweep time and NVMe copy latency. Snippet:
```
kv_evict_sweep: mean=3.4ms, p99=27ms
nvme_cp: mean=0.85ms/chunk(64KB), p99=5.2ms
```
On A100/eu-west1 nvme p99 is ~2x worse than h100/us-west1 which matches the p99 gap.

lin: Good find. Suggest adding an adaptive prefetch throttle: lower prefetch when nvme_p99 > 4ms or paging_bw < 300MB/s. That would keep p99 bounded.

raja: Agreed. Also add a runtime kernel selector that prefers fused path on H100 and falls back to cutlass on A100 until we can optimize chunk copy. I'll open a ticket and run the grid.

sam: FYI, turned on a short canary with prefetch=0.65 on eu-west1 A100 — initial p99 dropped from 118ms to ~86ms, hit rate stable 0.75. Looks promising. :thumbsup:

raja: Next steps: (1) run full grid, (2) add adaptive prefetch heuristic to runtime, (3) follow up kernel copy optimizations for A100. I'll file the follow-up: https://redwood.internal/issue/INF-8421 — assign to eng-ml. Thanks all. :eyes:
